factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon's public audit index lists Phase-1, Genesis, V2, and V4 engagements, and the public repository lists v4.3.0 as latest. However, no public artifact binds the running Genesis-chain binary or v4.3.0 source commit to a specific audited commit/build. Audit-to-deployment parity is therefore unverified.

The newest publicly accessible full-scope audit evidence is the Informal Systems Genesis V2 report from June 2025, approximately 13 months before this assessment. Babylon's public changelog shows later v4.2.x and v4.3.0 fixes, while referenced V4 audit reports are not publicly available for scope comparison. This exceeds the 12-month recency boundary for a high-value live protocol.

Zellic 2025 Genesis Chain audit: 32 findings (7 critical) — stated 'all resolved or acknowledged' but individual resolution commits for the 7 critical findings are not individually verifiable from accessible public secondary sources (PDF binary-encoded). OZ April 2026 findings: all 4 confirmed fixed (PR #584 jailing bypass, PR #1911 type assertion, plus 2 additional fixes per OZ blog). Informal Systems V2: 14 findings, all addressed. No 'Resolved' label without code change detected in accessible evidence.

Babylon's public audit index identifies multiple firms and engagements, but the available public evidence does not map the current Genesis deployment or all live components to the audited builds. The number of independent firms covering currently deployed code cannot therefore be established under the v1.7.0 definition.

Public sources identify recognized security organizations in Babylon's audit history, but current-deployment coverage is not established and no public source supplies the rubric's tier classification. This factor remains gray rather than inferring a positive tier result from a historical firm list.

Public audit reports provide engagement dates, but no public release/build manifest maps the current v4.3.0 Genesis deployment to those audited commits. A reliable audit-end-to-deployment interval cannot be calculated for the active code.

Active Immunefi bug bounty since September 2024. Maximum payout $500,000 (Critical). Covers 17 assets including Genesis chain, Bitcoin Indexer, Finality Provider, Vigilante, Covenant Emulator. KYC required. Notable exclusion: centralization risks and covenant committee compromise explicitly out of scope. $500K max is below peer expectation for $4.16B TVL.

Babylon publishes a 48-hour acknowledgement target and OpenZeppelin describes remediation of its reported findings. These sources support a documented process and one response, but cannot establish that no bounty disclosure has ever been ignored before exploitation.

No formal verification (Certora, TLA+, Kani, Coq) has been applied to Babylon's custom modules (x/btcstaking, x/finality, EOTS) from publicly available sources. Informal Systems uses formal analysis techniques but their V2 audit was a security audit, not a machine-verified FV proof engagement. Novel cryptographic primitives (EOTS, covenant committee Schnorr multisig) would benefit most from FV. No Certora/Kani proofs publicly available.

Primary codebase is Go (Genesis chain) and Rust (CosmWasm contracts). Standard DeFi static analyzers (Slither, Mythril) do not apply. Go-specific tools (staticcheck, gosec) and Rust tools (cargo-audit) are standard CI but no published automated tool-run output found for Babylon's custom modules. Zellic and Coinspect audits performed manual security review as substitute. Tool run not performed in this assessment.

SELFDESTRUCT opcode is an EVM Solidity construct. Babylon's execution environments (Bitcoin script, Cosmos SDK Go modules, CosmWasm Rust) have no equivalent. Bitcoin UTXOs can only be spent via valid script paths. Cosmos SDK modules persist via the KV store. CosmWasm contracts can be halted/migrated by admin but have no self-destruct equivalent.

EVM delegatecall opcode does not exist in Go (Cosmos SDK) or Rust (CosmWasm) execution contexts. Factor is structurally inapplicable. The analogous CosmWasm SubMsg pattern uses typed Rust messages, not arbitrary calldata. No evidence of uncontrolled SubMsg with user-supplied contract addresses in cosmos-bsn-contracts.

EVM arbitrary .call(target, data) pattern does not exist in Go/Rust contexts. Cosmos SDK uses MsgServer interfaces for inter-module calls. CosmWasm uses typed Rust enum messages. Babylon's Genesis chain has permissioned CosmWasm deployment (not permissionless), further limiting arbitrary contract invocation surfaces.

EVM-style reentrancy (callback-based re-entry before state commit) does not apply to Cosmos SDK Go execution model (atomic transaction processing, state commits after full handler completion) or CosmWasm (VM-level reentrancy guard in reply pattern). Factor as defined is structurally inapplicable.
ERC-777/ERC-1155/ERC-721 token standards do not exist in Cosmos SDK / CosmWasm ecosystem. BABY token is a native Cosmos denomination (ubbn). BTC is not tokenized. Factor structurally inapplicable.

Slither divide-before-multiply detector applies to Solidity only. Babylon is Go and Rust. The factor concept (integer arithmetic precision) applies to Go but no Go-specific published analysis found. Manual review of x/finality voting power calculations and x/btcstaking satoshi-denomination arithmetic would be required. No published finding on this topic from Zellic/Coinspect audits found.

Babylon documents BABY as 6-decimal ubbn and uses BTC-side satoshis, but no public static-analysis result or audit assertion verifies all cross-denomination arithmetic paths. The architecture does not itself prove the absence of a mixed-decimals defect.

Signed/unsigned confusion is a Solidity-specific class of vulnerability (implicit type conversions). Babylon Genesis chain uses Go (strict explicit conversion required) and Cosmos SDK math.Int wrapper for token amounts. CosmWasm contracts use Rust (strict type system, no implicit conversions). The vulnerability class does not exist in this toolchain. Structural N/A by non-Solidity substrate.

ecrecover is an EVM precompile for ECDSA signature recovery. Babylon uses Schnorr signatures (BIP-340) for Bitcoin operations, Cosmos SDK amino/protobuf signing for Genesis chain, and EOTS for finality provider double-sign detection. No ecrecover usage exists in this non-EVM architecture.

EIP-712 is an Ethereum structured-data signing standard. Babylon does not use EIP-712 anywhere. Bitcoin-side signing uses Taproot (BIP-341). Genesis chain uses Cosmos SDK SIGN_MODE_DIRECT which includes chain-ID (bbn-1) in the SignDoc by construction. Structurally inapplicable.

UUPS (EIP-1822) is an EVM proxy upgrade pattern. Babylon has no EVM contracts. Chain upgrades on Genesis proceed via Cosmos SDK x/gov software upgrade proposals — a governance vote is required before the upgrade handler executes. Structurally inapplicable.

Cosmos SDK modules use InitGenesis() for initial state setup, callable only at chain genesis block. CosmWasm contracts use instantiate() enforced as single-call by the CosmWasm VM. No Solidity initialize() pattern exists in this architecture. Structurally inapplicable.

OZ _disableInitializers() is an EVM Solidity pattern for upgradeable proxy impl contracts. Babylon has no EVM contracts. Cosmos SDK genesis initialization is structurally protected at the framework level. CosmWasm initialization semantics are enforced at VM level. Structurally inapplicable.

Babylon spans custom Cosmos SDK modules, Bitcoin-staking cryptography, off-chain services, and CosmWasm integration contracts. The public Zellic report recorded seven critical findings, and the public audit index does not identify a matching audit for every repository/component. The available evidence supports a yellow complexity-versus-audit-coverage concern.

Dual-layer governance: (a) BABY governance via Cosmos SDK x/gov — DAO model with 3-day voting period, 33.4% quorum, >50% threshold; no single admin key; (b) Bitcoin-layer: covenant committee 6-of-9 federated multisig for BTC unbonding co-signing. All software upgrades require on-chain governance vote (MsgSoftwareUpgrade). V2 upgrade (Jun 2025) and V4 upgrade (Nov 2025) both went through governance proposals confirmed by on-chain voting.

BABY governance is stake-weighted and the Bitcoin-side covenant committee has nine published public keys with a 6-of-9 quorum. The published committee mapping assigns three keys to Babylon Labs and the other six to named external organizations. The role count and threshold are not low-threshold multisig posture; organizational concentration is assessed separately under RD-F-029.

No single EOA or private key holds unilateral chain upgrade authority. Babylon Genesis software upgrades require on-chain BABY governance vote (MsgSoftwareUpgrade). V2 upgrade (proposal Jun 12, 2025 → activation Jun 16) and V4 upgrade (Proposal #18, Nov 2025) both confirmed as governance-voted. No Cosmos SDK crisis module sudo-admin key identified. Babylon Foundation holds significant BABY supply but cannot unilaterally execute upgrades.

bbn-1 parameters publish nine covenant keys and a 6-of-9 quorum. A six-signature threshold is not a low-threshold multisig relative to the nine-key set; Babylon Labs' three-key organizational concentration is a separate co-hosting/custody concern assessed under RD-F-029.

Covenant committee: 7 distinct organizations. Babylon Labs holds 3/9 keys — organizational co-hosting risk within Babylon Labs is inherent. Other 6 keys distributed across 6 independent organizations (AltLayer, CoinSummer, Cubist, Informal Systems, RockX, Zellic). ASN-level infrastructure data for Bitcoin Schnorr key custodians not available. Partial independence confirmed by organizational diversity; within-org co-hosting for Babylon Labs 3 keys is a yellow finding.

Covenant committee signers hold compressed Schnorr public keys for Bitcoin co-signing — these are offline keys for a federated signing service, not EVM hot wallets. On-chain behavioral heuristics (nonce velocity, gas jitter) are inapplicable to Bitcoin Schnorr keys. BABY governance is DAO-level; individual validator signing behavior for governance is not equivalent to multisig hot-wallet risk. Insufficient data to assess; structurally different from EVM hot-wallet pattern.

The public configuration publishes the current committee, but the available public sources do not provide a complete, independently verifiable 90-day signer-set event history. No conclusion on rotation recency or a threshold-reduction event is made from the static configuration alone.

No Ethereum TimelockController exists. Effective delay is the governance voting period: 3 days standard (72h) or 1 day expedited (24h). V2 upgrade used a 4-day window (proposal Jun 12 → activation Jun 16). V4 upgrade had 3-day voting period (Nov 10-13). 72h meets the green threshold (≥48h) for standard proposals, but expedited path allows 24h. Graded yellow: expedited path is structurally available and reduces effective timelock to 24h for certain proposals.

All sensitive actions (software upgrades, parameter changes, mint/inflation parameters, fee parameters) route through BABY governance module. No bypass path for normal operations. However: (a) no separate timelock delay after voting ends — execution is at the specified block height immediately after vote passes; (b) expedited proposals reduce delay to 24h with higher threshold (66.7%). No rescue/emergency function exists (structurally inapplicable). Oracle not applicable (no price oracle). Governance covers all actions but expedited path reduces delay.

No EVM-style pause-keeper role identified. No equivalent to EigenLayer's Pauser Multisig found for Babylon Genesis. Chain halt would require 2/3+ validator consensus (Cosmos SDK crisis module). IBC rate-limiter (V2 upgrade) provides partial circuit-breaker for cross-chain outflows (10%/24h) but is not an admin-controlled pause. The concept of a guardian role distinct from the upgrader (governance) is architecturally absent in this pure on-chain governance model.

All role types (upgrade, fee parameters, oracle config) are governed by the same BABY governance module — no separate role holders. Oracle is not applicable (no price oracle in core protocol). Upgrade role = governance. Fee parameters changed via governance (Proposal #8 reduced unbonding fees). Role separation is structurally absent in a pure on-chain governance model without granular role contracts. Not a data gap — structural architecture of Cosmos SDK x/gov.

Cosmos SDK x/gov uses bonded BABY (delegated to validators) as voting power, not spot token balance. Tokens must be bonded (staked/delegated) for voting power — requires the staking bonding period. Liquid BABY cannot be flash-loaned into governance voting weight in a single transaction. Voting power is determined by bonded delegation state at proposal creation block. No flash-loan vector identified in this architecture.

Not applicable — BABY governance uses bonded stake (not liquid tokens). Flash loans cannot acquire bonded voting power in Cosmos SDK. The quorum concept applies to bonded BABY participation, not liquid token acquisition. No flash-loan quorum manipulation vector exists in this architecture.

Standard proposals: 3-day voting period = 72h. Expedited proposals: 1-day voting period = 24h. Standard path meets the green threshold (≥48h). Expedited path (24h) is at the exact yellow/green boundary (24-47h = yellow). Graded yellow because the expedited path (24h) is explicitly available and structurally accessible for time-sensitive proposals with higher approval threshold (66.7%).

Cosmos SDK governance executes typed Protobuf messages through the module router (MsgUpdateParams, MsgSoftwareUpgrade, etc.). No EVM-style delegatecall or arbitrary call(target, calldata) in governance execution. Each proposal type maps to a typed handler routed to the relevant module keeper. No user-supplied target address, no delegatecall attack surface in Cosmos SDK governance architecture.

Cosmos SDK governance has NoWithVeto — if ≥33.4% of voting power votes NoWithVeto, proposal is rejected and deposit burned. This is an embedded veto mechanism within the voting period. However, there is no separate veto-only multisig entity. Effective veto requires organizing 33.4% of bonded BABY within 3 days. Foundation + investors hold ~66.5% of total supply; with first cliff passed (April 2026), insider concentration could theoretically pass or veto any proposal. Community veto depends on insider non-participation.

Not applicable. Bitcoin staking UTXOs can move only through their defined timelock, unbonding, and slashing script paths; this assessed surface does not expose an EVM-style admin rescue or emergencyWithdraw function.

Babylon documents a 10 billion initial BABY supply, 5.5% annual inflation, and on-chain governance. These materials establish a governed inflation model, but do not independently establish an admin-callable unlimited mint function or its cap semantics; the critical unlimited-mint condition is therefore not assessed.
factor_scores.notes: Public documentation does not establish an admin-callable unlimited mint function or its cap semantics.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. Babylon Genesis is initialized at chain genesis and governed through the Cosmos SDK governance module; the deployed-system condition of a contract deployer EOA retaining admin after seven days does not map to this chain architecture.

No EVM admin wallet exists. Covenant committee members hold Bitcoin Schnorr keys — their interaction history on Bitcoin is not equivalent to EVM wallet transaction history. Babylon Foundation holds BABY tokens in Cosmos SDK accounts, not monitorable EVM addresses. No Chainalysis-style feed data available for Bitcoin Schnorr keys or Cosmos-native accounts. Structural data gap for non-EVM architecture.

Cosmos SDK upgrades use on-chain MsgSoftwareUpgrade proposals with declared upgrade height and plan JSON. V2 (Jun 12 proposal → Jun 16 activation) and V4 (Proposal #18, Nov 2025) both had on-chain proposals. However, independent verification of upgrade-plan-declared-binary vs. actually-deployed binary not performed at this tier. The Cosmos SDK upgrade mechanism is inherently transparent (on-chain proposal with version string), but binary hash attestation was not independently verified.

Etherscan/Sourcify is EVM-specific and structurally inapplicable. Babylon Genesis is Cosmos SDK — all source code is public Go on GitHub (https://github.com/babylonlabs-io/babylon). Audited by Coinspect, Zellic, Informal Systems, Oak Security, Halborn (multiple public PDFs available). CosmWasm contracts are public Rust (cosmos-bsn-contracts repo). No closed-source binary for core modules. Protocol was not deployed with hidden contracts. Equivalent of 'verified source' is fully met.

Published tokenomics describes planned allocations and vesting, including Foundation-managed categories, early investors, team, advisors, and community incentives. It does not provide a current on-chain top-holder distribution, a bonded/delegated BABY voting-power distribution, or a reproducible Gini calculation. Current governance-power concentration is therefore not assessed.
factor_scores.notes: Public allocation and vesting plans are not evidence of current holder or bonded/delegated voting-power concentration.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Public review of Babylon's staking architecture and protocol source found no external price-feed integration: the BTC staking design uses native Bitcoin scripts and Babylon Genesis coordinates staking state rather than valuing collateral through an oracle. No asset/market requiring a price oracle was identified.
No price-oracle provider or priced market was identified in the reviewed core staking architecture, so there are no primary, secondary, or fallback oracle roles to assign.

The documented dependency map includes Bitcoin consensus and the Babylon Genesis chain, Vigilante infrastructure for Bitcoin/Genesis synchronization, and the covenant committee for protocol-compliant staking transactions. The public materials describe these dependencies, but do not publish a complete operator inventory or all operational dependency relationships; the dependency graph is therefore only partially documented.
This factor concerns the failure behavior of a price oracle. Babylon's reviewed native-Bitcoin staking path does not consume a price oracle, so no oracle fallback path applies.

Public documentation permits a bounded breakage assessment: a Vigilante outage can delay Bitcoin/Genesis synchronization, while a covenant-quorum outage can prevent protocol-compliant staking signatures. Babylon documents that a dishonest covenant supermajority cannot steal BTC, but it can refuse co-signatures. These are material liveness impairments, so the dependency impact is partially adverse rather than gracefully degraded.
No DEX pool price is used by the reviewed native-Bitcoin staking path; a spot-DEX oracle assessment is structurally inapplicable.
Babylon's reviewed core staking path does not consume a DEX-TWAP oracle, leaving no TWAP window to measure.
No DEX pool is used as an oracle in the reviewed core staking path, so oracle-pool depth is inapplicable.
No DEX-pool price source was identified in Babylon's reviewed core staking architecture, so single-pool medianization does not apply.
Babylon's reviewed core staking architecture has no price-oracle read, so an in-protocol price-deviation circuit breaker is inapplicable.
No price-deviation circuit breaker is required because no oracle price is consumed by the reviewed core staking path.
The reviewed core staking path has no external price feed whose update time could become stale; oracle-staleness checking is inapplicable.
Babylon's reviewed core staking architecture does not use a Chainlink aggregator, making Chainlink min/max-bound handling inapplicable.
Babylon is a native Bitcoin staking protocol rather than a lending protocol; no LP-token collateral-pricing path was identified.

Vigilantes are documented as decentralized, without centralized coordination, and operators can run the program. The public material does not enumerate a live independent operator set or prove operational redundancy at the assessment date, leaving a liveness-redundancy gap.

As checked 2026-07-24, DefiLlama reports $3.349B TVL, entirely on Bitcoin, and a 4.2% 30-day increase. This exceeds the rubric's $100M scale threshold. The single-asset BTC composition is a disclosed concentration consideration but does not negate the protocol's current absolute scale.

Babylon's published TVL is entirely Bitcoin and each stake delegates to a selected Finality Provider, but no independently verifiable public dataset reports the rubric's top-10 BTC-staker share. The required wallet-concentration measure therefore remains unquantified rather than supporting a directional concentration claim.
factor_scores.notes: Gray: public sources establish the staking/delegation model but do not publish a top-10 depositor-share calculation.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon's protocol-held BTC is locked in staking-script outputs rather than a protocol-native DEX pool. The public specification requires an on-demand unbonding transaction and a covenant-threshold signing path; no independently verifiable 2%/5% liquidity-depth metric is published for the staked BTC. This is a yellow exit-liquidity evidence and process constraint.

Not applicable. Babylon's documented core is BTC and BABY staking, finality provision, and Bitcoin-script coordination; it does not document borrow markets from which a borrowed-to-supplied utilization rate could be calculated.
factor_scores.notes: Babylon is not a lending protocol and has no borrowing markets in the approved protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. This factor measures lender-socialized bad debt. Babylon's published design is a BTC/BABY staking and shared-security system, not a lending market with supplier and borrower balances.
factor_scores.notes: No lending-market bad-debt mechanism is present in the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. Babylon's published BTC staking design locks BTC in script-controlled outputs to secure PoS networks; it does not extend loans against collateral or expose a lending collateralization ratio.
factor_scores.notes: No collateralized borrowing market is present in the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. BABY is Babylon Genesis's native gas, governance, and staking token, not a stablecoin; the protocol does not issue an algorithmic or under-collateralized stablecoin in its documented core design.
factor_scores.notes: No stablecoin issuance is part of the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. RD-F-070 concerns a listed Compound V2-style lending market with zero supply and zero borrow. Babylon's documented staking transaction locks BTC in a Taproot output and its coordination layer is a Cosmos SDK chain; no cToken lending market is part of this protocol surface.
factor_scores.notes: Critical factor does not apply because Babylon has no Compound V2-style lending markets or share-based cToken accounting.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. RD-F-071 evaluates seed-deposit requirements for a new lending-market listing. Babylon's documented protocol provides BTC staking, Finality Provider delegation, and Genesis coordination rather than lender and borrower market creation.
factor_scores.notes: No lending-market listing flow is part of the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. RD-F-072 evaluates the governance threshold for listing a lending market. Babylon governance covers protocol changes, upgrades, smart-contract deployments, and parameters; this does not create a lending-market listing surface.
factor_scores.notes: No lending-market governance listing mechanism is part of the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. RD-F-073 assesses whether a lending asset's borrow cap is robust to oracle manipulation. Babylon's documented core uses BTC staking scripts and Cosmos SDK coordination, without a borrow-cap or lending-oracle surface.
factor_scores.notes: No lending borrow cap or asset-pricing oracle is part of the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. RD-F-074 assesses the virtual-share offset in ERC-4626 vaults. Babylon's published architecture uses Bitcoin scripts for staking and a Cosmos SDK coordination layer, not an ERC-4626 vault or Solidity share-accounting system.
factor_scores.notes: No ERC-4626 vault is part of the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Not applicable. RD-F-075 assesses first-depositor or share-inflation protection in a vault. Babylon's BTC stakes are individually created Taproot outputs with defined spending paths, not deposits into a share-minting vault.
factor_scores.notes: No share-minting vault or first-depositor mechanism is part of the approved Babylon protocol surface.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Phase-1 BTC staking layer live since 2024-08-22 (~621 days to assessment date). Genesis chain live since 2025-04-10 (~389 days). Primary TVL-bearing surface (Phase-1 Bitcoin UTXOs) clears 365-day threshold. Both layers exceed the minimum green threshold.

The prior zero-exploit conclusion lacked independently verifiable, factor-specific public support. Current public research confirms security findings but does not establish an exhaustive financial-loss history. A public incident ledger was not established in this pass.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The public DeFiLlama protocol API supplied 90 daily TVL observations ending 2026-07-24. The population coefficient of variation is 0.1364 (mean $3.61B), below the v1.7.0 green threshold of 0.15.
No public factor-specific incident record established an applicable response-time measurement. The former conclusion depended on unsafe cached absence assertions.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon's public BTC-staking specification uses individually controlled Bitcoin transaction outputs and describes no protocol-level application pause control for those outputs. No independently verifiable public event log established a trailing-12-month activation count, so this remains gray.

The BTC-staking specification describes timelock, unbonding, slashing, and withdrawal paths rather than an application pause control. Public evidence reviewed does not establish the duration of any protocol pause event, so this factor remains gray.

The Babylon Genesis V2 post documents a software upgrade, but public material reviewed does not provide a complete deployment-address inventory over the trailing year. It cannot establish the factor's no-redeployment conclusion.
factor_scores.notes: A complete public deployment-address history for the trailing-year test was not established in this refresh.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No active qualifying Babylon cover was established by the cited public evidence. Babylon describes its Nexus Mutual product as upcoming/developing; Nexus Mutual's documented Protocol Cover is restricted to Ethereum, EVM-compatible networks, and L2s; Babylon's later Nexus/Native update discusses insurance primitives without identifying an active Babylon policy. Red.
factor_scores.notes: Independent review retained red using the bounded public evidence above; this does not assert a provider-wide absence beyond the cited products and announcements.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The mixer-to-protocol signal is applicable to Babylon's Bitcoin and Genesis-chain activity, but no public address-label feed or time-bounded interaction monitor establishes whether a recent mixer withdrawal touched the staking surface on 2026-07-24.
factor_scores.notes: A public CTI/cluster feed and protocol-address monitoring are required for a positive or negative firing determination.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon's BTC staking surface is identifiable, but no public, protocol-specific transaction classifier establishes a current baseline or detects small pre-drain transactions followed by a matching larger drain.
factor_scores.notes: This requires a Bitcoin/Genesis-chain transaction stream and a defined pre-strike pattern corpus.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon supports governance-mediated changes, but the public materials reviewed do not identify a canonical deployer wallet or provide an unconfirmed-transaction baseline for privileged Genesis-chain actors.
factor_scores.notes: A named privileged-address set plus mempool telemetry is required to assess an unusual sequence.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The rubric's attacker-wallet priority-fee threshold cannot be evaluated from the reviewed public materials because no Babylon-specific attacker label set, pending-transaction feed, or fee baseline was available.
factor_scores.notes: Bitcoin and Cosmos transaction fees do not supply the EVM priority-fee data assumed by this signal; a substrate-specific monitor would be needed.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No public similarity scanner or Babylon-specific exploit-template corpus was identified for newly deployed code or scripts, so a current bytecode/template match cannot be determined.
factor_scores.notes: The signal needs a maintained template corpus and a chain-appropriate deployment scanner.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: A current known-exploit call-pattern replay cannot be assessed: Babylon's public governance and protocol materials do not provide a live message-pattern monitor or an exploit-replay signature corpus.
factor_scores.notes: The signal requires protocol-specific transaction decoding and a maintained pattern library.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon's documented staking surface is self-custodial Bitcoin staking rather than an ERC-20 approval surface; an ERC-20 whale-approval signal is structurally mismatched.
factor_scores.notes: The factor specifically requires ERC-20 approvals to an unverified contract.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon has observable Bitcoin and Genesis-chain activity, but no public sybil-clustering result or short-window identical-transaction monitor was available for the assessed date.
factor_scores.notes: A defined transaction window, clustering methodology, and protocol-address scope are required.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: DefiLlama reported Babylon TVL of about $3.334B and a +3.8% 30-day change at retrieval; this public snapshot does not show the configured rapid TVL-drain condition firing.
factor_scores.notes: This is a point-in-time public TVL posture, not a substitute for an hourly canary.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No primary price oracle consumed by Babylon's documented Bitcoin staking and Genesis-governance flows was identified; an oracle-versus-secondary price-deviation signal is structurally mismatched to that surface.
factor_scores.notes: This does not assess third-party market pricing of BABY or BTC.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No public Babylon-specific flash-loan event feed or protocol-token flash-loan venue was identified that could establish whether a loan above the rubric threshold is currently targeting Babylon.
factor_scores.notes: A current event feed covering the relevant lending venues and Babylon-targeting transaction classification is required.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon documents a transparent on-chain proposal lifecycle with deposits, voting, and execution; no public evidence reviewed for 2026-07-24 identified a queued Babylon proposal with an adverse protocol-impactful payload.
factor_scores.notes: The governance process is observable; this finding is limited to the reviewed public proposal surfaces.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Governance-mediated parameter and software changes are documented, but no public pending-transaction feed was available to determine whether an admin or upgrade transaction is presently awaiting confirmation.
factor_scores.notes: The factor is a pre-confirmation signal and requires a chain-specific mempool feed.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon documents a Covenant Committee responsible for staking-transaction integrity, but no public change-feed or independently verified current-versus-prior signer-set diff was available to determine whether a signer-set change is proposed or executed.
factor_scores.notes: A committee-configuration history and proposal/event monitor are required for this real-time signal.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The reviewed Babylon TVL is entirely on Bitcoin and the protocol description is self-custodial Bitcoin staking; no stablecoin shared-liquidity dependency was identified for a depeg signal.
factor_scores.notes: This conclusion concerns Babylon's protocol dependency graph, not unrelated venues that list BABY.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Babylon publishes a staking application and public frontend source, but no published prior bundle hash, DNS-history baseline, or continuous change monitor was available to determine current frontend or DNS drift.
factor_scores.notes: A trusted prior hash and DNS observation history are required to fire this signal.

go.mod pins exact versions for all critical dependencies: Cosmos SDK v0.53.5, CometBFT v0.38.22, CosmWasm/wasmd v0.60.5, IBC-Go v10.5.0, btcd v0.24.2. go.sum provides cryptographic hashes for all 1,629 dependency entries. cosmos-bsn-contracts Cargo.lock pins all Rust dependencies to exact versions (cosmwasm-std 2.2.2, bitcoin 0.32.6, k256). No floating/unpinned version ranges observed.

The public go.mod and go.sum provide dependency pinning and checksums, but no authoritative, exhaustive public incident feed was located that can prove the absence of a malicious dependency release across the full dependency graph during the trailing 90 days.

CometBFT GHSA-h598-3g3g-c67c: patched in v4.2.5 (current v4.2.7 is patched). Babylon also issued 4 own GHSAs in 2025-2026 (vote extension, BIP-322 sig, nil pointer, AfterBtcDelegationUnbonded hook) — all patched in v4.1.0–v4.2.0. cosmwasm-std RUSTSEC-2024-0338 (arithmetic overflow in pow/neg): affects <2.0.2; Cargo.lock pins 2.2.2 (patched). RUSTSEC-2024-0361 (gas mispricing, affects <2.1.3): 2.2.2 is patched. No open critical library vulnerabilities in current deployed versions, but the volume of self-issued GHSAs in 2025-2026 indicates active vulnerability surface in the chain modules.

The July 21, 2026 v4.3.1 release tag is signed and publishes platform binaries with SHA-256 checksums. That supports release provenance, but public evidence reviewed does not bind the currently running Babylon Genesis binary to that tag or independently compare its runtime artifact with the release commit.

The public release list shows ongoing code releases, including v4.3.1 on July 21, 2026, but release publication does not establish the count of Babylon Genesis upgrades actually activated on-chain in the trailing 90 days. A public on-chain upgrade-event history was not independently verified for this review.

The release history shows v4.3.1 published on July 21, 2026, but it does not establish whether any software or configuration change was activated on Babylon Genesis through or outside the documented governance path in the trailing 30 days. No public chain-level hot-patch event history was independently verified.

GitHub lists signed v4.3.1 as the latest July 21, 2026 release, while Babylon's audit documentation and OpenZeppelin's April 2026 research establish public review activity. The reviewed public material does not link the latest released or running code to a post-change audit scope, nor does it independently prove that a material unaudited release is live; yellow records that unresolved coverage gap.
factor_scores.notes: Latest release-to-audit and release-to-running-chain mappings were not publicly established.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: OpenZeppelin reports that Babylon Labs confirmed and triaged its findings and shipped fixes promptly. The public release history confirms later releases, but the reviewed public evidence does not map each disclosed fix to the currently running chain binary; an unresolved merged-but-not-deployed gap cannot be excluded.

Official governance documentation lists the intended deposit, voting-period, quorum, and threshold parameters, and the V2 announcement describes its rollout. Those sources do not independently attest the full currently deployed chain configuration or exclude all test-mode parameters across modules.

Not applicable. Cosmos SDK uses module-keyed key/value store (IAVL tree), not EIP-1967 proxy storage slots. No Solidity storage layouts or slot assignment conflicts exist. Module upgrades use Cosmos SDK RegisterMigration and ConsensusVersion patterns, not EVM storage slot migration. The EVM storage-layout collision risk class is architecturally absent.

_disableInitializers() is an OpenZeppelin Solidity pattern for EIP-1967 proxied contracts. Cosmos SDK modules use Go constructors and module genesis init functions, which are one-time operations at chain genesis — not re-callable via a separate initializer function. No proxy pattern, no delegatecall, no Solidity initializer exists in Cosmos SDK. The concept of proxy re-initialization is architecturally absent.

CREATE2 is an EVM opcode. Cosmos SDK and Bitcoin do not use CREATE2. CosmWasm contract deployment uses code IDs and instantiation, not CREATE2 patterns. No same-address redeploy risk exists in this architecture.

The public repository publishes tagged source and release artifacts. However, the reviewed public material does not provide a reproducible-build attestation or an independent reproduction matching a deployed Babylon Genesis binary, so bytecode reproducibility remains unverified.

The public release record includes v4.3.1 on July 21, 2026, but it does not provide a complete chain-level inventory of new Babylon protocol deployments or CosmWasm instantiations in the trailing 30 days. The number of fresh deployed attack surfaces is not independently assessed.

Babylon coordinates Bitcoin and Babylon Genesis through the Vigilante components, and its staking state is represented on both networks. This is a cross-chain coordination surface even though the documented design uses native BTC staking rather than wrapped-asset custody.

Babylon's Phase-1 public launch documentation identifies a 6-of-9 covenant committee, including three Babylon Labs keys. That is a small signer set for a material BTC staking surface. Current public documentation confirms the committee's multisig role but does not provide a complete independently verifiable current signer roster, so this is assessed yellow rather than assuming a larger current set.

Official launch documentation specifies a 6-of-9 covenant threshold. This is a BFT-style quorum, but Babylon Labs held three of the documented nine keys, and the current public materials do not independently establish the present signer distribution; the threshold/concentration position is therefore yellow.

The public operator documentation describes isolated covenant-signer components but does not disclose committee-member hosting, ASN, cloud, or data-center arrangements. Co-hosting cannot be independently determined from public evidence.

The reviewed cross-chain path is built from Bitcoin scripts, covenant public keys, and Babylon Genesis coordination rather than an EVM bridge verifier. An Ethereum ecrecover return-address check is structurally inapplicable.

The documented cross-chain coordination path is bound to Bitcoin and Babylon Genesis: Vigilantes relay between those named networks and staking transactions include the BTC network as a protocol field. No generic shared-signer message path lacking origin binding was identified.

Bitcoin staking is represented by individual Bitcoin transaction outputs with specific spending conditions, and Babylon documents validation/indexing of those transactions. The reviewed design uses this one-use UTXO model rather than an inbox that accepts a message repeatedly, providing an equivalent replay barrier for the documented staking path.

The reviewed architecture uses Bitcoin UTXO spending paths and covenant signatures, not a Merkle-root inbox or a root-acceptance mapping. The bytes32(0) bridge-root pattern is structurally inapplicable.

Public documentation says changing the covenant committee requires governance, but no dated public rotation or complete signer-set history sufficient to measure recency was located. Rotation recency is therefore not independently assessable.

The public launch announcement identifies organizational key holders, but no public evidence establishes the actual key-custody provider, cloud KMS, or hardware custody relationships across committee members. Shared-custody concentration cannot be determined.

RD-F-157 measures TVL locked in a bridge contract divided by that bridge's validator count. Babylon's documented design uses native Bitcoin staking and self-custodial Bitcoin-script spending conditions, while the covenant committee enforces protocol-compliant staking rules and cannot steal staker BTC. No bridge contract or bridge-specific locked-value numerator was identified; the protocol-wide TVL dashboard is not scope-equivalent evidence for this factor. The bridge-TVL-per-validator metric is therefore inapplicable.

No public, protocol-scoped threat-actor cluster attribution was available to determine whether a known DPRK/Lazarus or other threat-actor cluster has touched Babylon's Bitcoin or Genesis-chain activity.
factor_scores.notes: A vetted cluster-label feed and explicit protocol-address inventory are required; absence of a search result is not a green finding.

Not applicable. The assessed Bitcoin staking surface uses user-controlled Taproot UTXOs with defined timelock, unbonding, and slashing paths; no deprecated paused protocol contract with a live admin-controlled reversible pause has been identified.

Not applicable. ERC-20 approvals and router patterns are EVM concepts. BABY is a native Cosmos denomination (ubbn), not an ERC-20. No EVM-style approve/transferFrom allowances exist. No deprecated router contracts on bbn-1 identified. Structurally inapplicable to this architecture.

Babylon's public go.mod specifies Go 1.25.8. Go's release archive lists newer 1.25.10 and 1.26.4 releases. No public evidence here establishes a directly applicable compiler defect, but the maintained source is multiple patches behind its stated Go series; this supports yellow rather than green.

Babylon is an original protocol with no upstream DeFi fork. Bitcoin staking script, EOTS cryptographic primitive, and Genesis chain modules implement novel functionality. No high-bytecode-similarity-with-behavior-deviation pattern is applicable.

Public commit-message searches cannot reliably establish whether AI tools co-authored security-critical code. No positive disclosure was located, but absence of a commit-message marker is not sufficient to score green.

No public Babylon disclosure reviewed identifies AI-generated code in security-critical paths. Public repository history alone cannot establish whether AI tools were used, so this factor remains gray rather than inferring a favorable result from silence.

Go 1.25.x: not EOL (Go supports current + one prior major version; 1.26 is current, 1.25 is in maintenance with security support). Rust edition 2021: active support. CometBFT v0.38.22: actively patched (security releases through 2026). Cosmos SDK v0.53.5: actively maintained. CosmWasm/wasmd v0.60.5: maintained CosmWasm v2 series. No EOL toolchain or compiler version in the dependency chain.

Babylon has a live, triaged Immunefi program and publishes both security@babylonlabs.io and GitHub private vulnerability reporting. OpenZeppelin's public research describes Babylon's prompt coordinated-disclosure response. These are public disclosure channels with recent response evidence.

SECURITY.md explicitly states: 'We will confirm receipt of your report within 48 hours.' This is a published SLA under the 72-hour green threshold. However, no public record exists of this SLA being tested and verified under a real-world disclosure scenario (OZ 2026 disclosure was actioned but no timestamps published). Yellow = SLA stated but not verified through prior instances.

Public research supports prompt handling of particular disclosed vulnerabilities, but it does not establish a complete record of every disclosure or whether any prior disclosure was ignored before exploitation.
factor_scores.notes: No public, exhaustive disclosure and exploitation ledger was established in this refresh.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Public GitHub advisories identify three Babylon repository vulnerabilities: malformed vote extensions (moderate, patched in v4.1.0), nil BlockHash consensus panics (high, patched in v4.2.0), and BIP-322 compliance (low, patched in v4.1.0). Advisory issuance with stated fixes supports yellow.

No LayerZero OFT adapter is described in the reviewed Babylon staking and cross-chain coordination materials; the documented mechanism is Vigilante synchronization between Bitcoin and Babylon Genesis. LayerZero DVN configuration is inapplicable.

No price-oracle address or oracle-binding mechanism was identified in the reviewed native-Bitcoin core staking path. Because the protocol does not consume a collateral price oracle, immutable-oracle-address risk is inapplicable.
Babylon is documented as a Bitcoin staking protocol, not a lending protocol that accepts collateral prices from permissionlessly created pools. This lending-oracle pattern is inapplicable.

Babylon documents a Covenant Committee and governance-mediated network changes, but no public real-time configuration-diff or proposal alert establishes a current threshold reduction or comparable governance weakening event.
factor_scores.notes: A current committee/quorum parameter baseline and change monitor are required.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Immunefi program explicitly excludes 'centralization risks' and 'covenant committee compromise scenarios' from scope. The covenant committee (6-of-9 federated multisig) co-signs all BTC unbonding transactions and is the primary security primitive protecting $4.16B in staked BTC. Its explicit exclusion from bug bounty scope creates a meaningful protection gap for the protocol's highest-value surface. cosmos-bsn-contracts not clearly enumerated as in-scope assets.

The reviewed public materials identify the founders and document the protocol architecture, but they do not provide a complete, independently verifiable dataset for detecting a real-capital social-engineering persona pattern. No factor-specific favorable or adverse conclusion is supported.

POSITIVE FINDING: V2 upgrade (June 2025) added IBC rate limiting capping BABY token exits at 10% of native supply within 24 hours — explicit outflow rate-limiter. No admin-triggered chain-level pause mechanism identified (Cosmos SDK x/crisis is validator-consensus-based halt, not admin key). Score yellow: rate-limiter present (positive) but no admin-triggered chain-pause capability separate from consensus. The rate-limiter is a material security mitigant for cross-chain outflow risk.

family.description: BTC restaking protocol enabling self-custodial Bitcoin staking via Taproot covenant scripts on Bitcoin mainnet, with a companion Cosmos SDK L1 (Babylon Genesis, chain-id bbn-1) serving as the accounting layer for BTC delegations, finality provider registry, and Bitcoin-secured network (BSN) provisioning. BTC stays on Bitcoin (locked in P2TR UTXOs); slashing is enforced via EOTS (Extractable One-Time Signatures) which expose finality provider private keys upon double-signing, enabling on-Bitcoin slashing. Covenant committee (6-of-9 federated multisig) co-signs unbonding transactions during Phase-2 covenant emulation period. Largest BTC DeFi protocol by TVL ($4.16B, 100% Bitcoin). Phase-1 launched August 22, 2024; Phase-2 / Genesis chain launched April 10, 2025.
